questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Commerce is best defined as
options: the growing of crops and rearing of animals
the process of taxing goods entering a country
all activities connected with the buying, selling, and exchange of goods, including the aids that facilitate this
questions.explanation: Commerce covers trade (buying and selling) plus the aids-to-trade (banking, insurance, transport, etc.) that make trade possible.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The two main branches into which commerce is divided are
questions.explanation: Commerce is broadly divided into trade (the actual buying and selling) and aids to trade (services that support trade).

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Which of the following is NOT classified as an aid to trade?
questions.explanation: Manufacturing is a form of production (industry), not a service that assists the movement or exchange of goods.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Trade may be broadly classified into
questions.explanation: Trade is divided into home (internal) trade, conducted within a country, and foreign (international) trade, conducted between countries.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Commerce serves as a link between
questions.explanation: Commerce bridges the gap between producers of goods and the final consumers by moving goods to where and when they are needed.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The exchange of goods for other goods without the use of money is known as
questions.explanation: Barter is the historical trading system in which goods are directly exchanged for other goods, without money as a medium.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: One major problem of the barter system was
options: lack of a common measure of value for goods being exchanged
questions.explanation: Under barter, there was no standard unit to measure the value of different goods, making fair exchange difficult.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The introduction of money into trade mainly helped to solve the barter problem of
questions.explanation: Money removed the need for a 'double coincidence of wants' — where each trader must want exactly what the other offers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Which of these is an example of an aid to trade?
questions.explanation: Insurance is a service (aid to trade) that supports commerce by covering risks; farming, fishing, and mining are extractive/production activities.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The main function of commerce in an economy is to
options: manufacture finished goods from raw materials
extract raw materials from the earth
remove the hindrances that stand between producers and consumers
control the value of a country's currency
questions.explanation: Commerce exists to overcome barriers of place, time, information, and risk that separate producers from consumers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The hindrance of trade concerned with goods being in the wrong place is overcome mainly by
questions.explanation: Transport moves goods from the place of production to the place of consumption, solving the hindrance of place.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The hindrance of trade concerned with goods not being available when needed is overcome mainly by
questions.explanation: Warehousing stores goods until they are needed, solving the hindrance of time.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The hindrance of trade concerned with buyers not knowing where to obtain goods is overcome mainly by
questions.explanation: Advertising informs potential buyers about the availability and source of goods, overcoming the hindrance of knowledge/information.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The hindrance of trade concerned with risk of loss or damage to goods is overcome mainly by
questions.explanation: Insurance provides financial protection against risks such as fire, theft, and accidents, overcoming the hindrance of risk.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The hindrance of trade concerned with the difficulty of paying for goods at a distance is overcome mainly by
questions.explanation: Banks provide payment and credit facilities that make it possible to settle transactions between distant parties, overcoming the hindrance of exchange of value.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Occupations can be broadly classified into
options: trade and aids to trade only
home trade and foreign trade only
industrial, commercial, professional, and personal service occupations
questions.explanation: Occupations are grouped into industrial (production), commercial (trade and aids to trade), professional, and personal service categories.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Industrial occupations that involve obtaining raw materials directly from nature are called
questions.explanation: Extractive occupations, such as mining and fishing, obtain raw materials directly from land, sea, or air.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Fishing, mining, and lumbering are examples of
questions.explanation: These occupations extract natural resources directly from the environment.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Building and civil engineering works are examples of
questions.explanation: Constructive occupations involve erecting structures such as buildings, roads, and bridges.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Turning raw materials such as cotton into finished goods such as cloth is an example of
questions.explanation: Manufacturing involves converting raw materials into finished or semi-finished products.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Commercial occupations include which of the following?
questions.explanation: Commercial occupations cover trade and the aids to trade, such as banking, insurance, and transport.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Which of the following is a professional occupation?
questions.explanation: Professional occupations require specialised training and expertise, such as medicine, law, and accountancy.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Hairdressing and catering are examples of
questions.explanation: Personal service occupations directly serve individuals, such as hairdressing, catering, and laundry services.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A major factor influencing a person's choice of occupation is
options: the type of currency in use
questions.explanation: People often choose occupations that match their interests, skills, and natural abilities.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Which of these best describes 'division of labour' as it relates to occupations?
options: Breaking a production process into separate tasks performed by different workers
Splitting a country into different trade regions
questions.explanation: Division of labour splits a job into specialised tasks, increasing efficiency and output.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A business owned and controlled by one person, who bears all the risks and enjoys all the profits, is called a
questions.explanation: A sole proprietorship is owned by a single individual who has full control and unlimited liability.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A major disadvantage of sole proprietorship is
questions.explanation: A sole trader is personally liable for all business debts, risking personal assets if the business fails.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: An association of two to twenty persons carrying on business together with a view to making profit is called a
questions.explanation: A partnership is formed by two or more people (subject to a maximum, traditionally twenty for ordinary trading partnerships) who share ownership and profit.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The document that governs the internal relationship between partners in a partnership is the
questions.explanation: The partnership deed (or agreement) sets out the terms agreed upon by partners, such as profit sharing and capital contribution.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: In the absence of a partnership agreement, profits and losses are shared
options: according to the age of each partner
according to the number of years in the business
questions.explanation: Under the Partnership Act, in the absence of an agreement, partners share profits and losses equally regardless of capital contributed.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A partner who takes an active part in the management of the business and has unlimited liability is called a
questions.explanation: A general partner participates actively in management and bears unlimited liability for the firm's debts.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A partner who contributes capital but takes no active part in management, with liability limited to their capital contribution, is called a
questions.explanation: A limited partner's liability is restricted to the amount of capital invested, and they do not take part in day-to-day management.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A company whose shares can be freely bought and sold on the stock exchange is called a
questions.explanation: A public limited company can offer its shares to the general public and list them on a stock exchange.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A company whose shares cannot be offered to the general public and are restricted in transfer is called a
questions.explanation: A private limited company restricts the transfer of its shares and cannot invite the public to subscribe for shares.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The document that contains a company's name, objectives, and relationship with the outside world is the
questions.explanation: The memorandum of association defines a company's name, objectives, and its relationship with outsiders.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The document that contains the internal rules and regulations governing a company's management is the
questions.explanation: The articles of association govern the internal management and administration of a company.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A legal document issued to the public inviting them to subscribe for shares in a company is called a
questions.explanation: A prospectus is an invitation to the public to buy shares or debentures of a company, containing relevant company information.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: An organisation owned and controlled by the government to provide essential services, often not solely for profit, is called a
questions.explanation: Public corporations, such as national electricity or water boards, are established by government to provide essential services to the public.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A business organisation formed by people with common interests who pool resources for mutual economic benefit is called a
questions.explanation: Cooperative societies are voluntary associations where members combine resources for shared economic benefits, often on a one-member-one-vote basis.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Capital that a company is legally permitted to raise, as stated in its memorandum of association, is called
questions.explanation: Authorized (or registered) capital is the maximum amount of share capital a company is allowed to raise, as stated in its memorandum.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The portion of authorized capital that a company has actually offered to shareholders is known as
questions.explanation: Issued capital refers to the part of the authorized capital that has been allotted to shareholders.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The part of the issued capital that shareholders have been asked to pay is called
questions.explanation: Called-up capital is the portion of the issued capital which the company has requested shareholders to pay.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The amount actually paid by shareholders on the shares called up is known as
questions.explanation: Paid-up capital is the amount of the called-up capital that shareholders have actually paid to the company.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Working capital is best described as
options: the total capital authorized by a company
the value of a company's fixed assets
the excess of current assets over current liabilities
the capital contributed by a sole owner only
questions.explanation: Working capital measures a business's short-term financial health, calculated as current assets minus current liabilities.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: One reason a partnership or company may be dissolved is
options: expansion of the business into new markets
an increase in the number of customers
mutual agreement of the owners to end the business
questions.explanation: Businesses are commonly dissolved by mutual agreement, insolvency, death of a partner, expiry of an agreed term, or court order.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The sale of goods in large quantities to retailers and other traders, rather than directly to final consumers, is called
questions.explanation: Wholesalers buy in bulk from producers and sell in smaller quantities to retailers, bridging producers and retailers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A major function of the wholesaler to the manufacturer is
options: buying in bulk, thereby relieving the manufacturer of storage and distribution costs
fixing the retail price of goods nationwide
questions.explanation: Wholesalers take bulk purchases off the manufacturer's hands, allowing manufacturers to focus on production rather than storage and distribution.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A major function of the wholesaler to the retailer is
options: breaking bulk into smaller quantities suitable for retailers
questions.explanation: Wholesalers break bulk purchases into smaller units that retailers can afford and manage, saving retailers storage space and capital.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The sale of goods directly to the final consumer in relatively small quantities is called
questions.explanation: Retail trade is the final stage of distribution, selling goods directly to consumers for personal use.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A large-scale retail organisation that sells a wide variety of goods under one roof, organised into different departments, is a
questions.explanation: Department stores offer a wide range of goods organised into separate departments within one large building.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Trade carried on between two or more countries is known as
questions.explanation: International trade involves the exchange of goods and services across national borders.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The bringing of goods into a country from abroad is called
questions.explanation: Import trade involves purchasing goods from other countries and bringing them into the home country.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The sending of goods from a country to other countries is called
questions.explanation: Export trade involves selling and sending goods produced at home to buyers in other countries.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Trade that involves importing goods into a country and re-exporting them to other countries, often after minor processing, is called
questions.explanation: Entrepot trade involves a country acting as a trading centre, importing goods for the purpose of re-exporting them.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A document that gives details of goods shipped, issued by the shipping company as evidence of a contract of carriage, is called a
questions.explanation: The bill of lading is issued by the shipowner/carrier as a receipt for goods shipped and evidence of the contract of carriage.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A document that certifies the country in which goods were manufactured or produced is called a
questions.explanation: A certificate of origin proves the country of manufacture of goods, often required for customs and tariff purposes.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A document showing the details, prices, and quantities of goods sold, sent by the seller to the buyer, is called an
questions.explanation: An invoice is a bill sent by the seller detailing the goods, quantities, and prices, and requesting payment.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: An invoice certified by the consul of the importing country, confirming the value and origin of goods, is called a
questions.explanation: A consular invoice is certified by the consulate of the importing country to verify the value and details of the exported goods, often to prevent under-invoicing.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A written order by one person (the drawer) directing another (the drawee) to pay a specified sum to a third party is called a
questions.explanation: A bill of exchange is a written, unconditional order to pay a specified sum of money, commonly used in settling international trade debts.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A tax imposed by a government on goods entering or leaving a country is called a
questions.explanation: Tariffs are taxes charged on imports (and sometimes exports) to raise revenue or protect local industries.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A restriction that limits the physical quantity of a commodity that may be imported into a country is called a
questions.explanation: A quota fixes the maximum quantity of a good that can be imported (or exported) within a given period.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A total ban placed by a government on trade with a particular country or on a particular commodity is called an
questions.explanation: An embargo is a complete prohibition on trade, often imposed for political or strategic reasons.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Government restrictions on the amount of foreign currency that can be bought, sold, or transferred are called
questions.explanation: Exchange control regulates the buying, selling, and holding of foreign currencies to manage a country's balance of payments.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The difference between the value of a country's visible exports and visible imports over a period is called the
questions.explanation: Balance of trade specifically compares visible (physical goods) exports and imports, unlike balance of payments which covers all transactions.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A record of all economic transactions between a country's residents and the rest of the world over a period is called the
questions.explanation: The balance of payments includes visible trade, invisible trade (services), and capital transactions, unlike the narrower balance of trade.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A financial institution that accepts deposits and grants loans to customers is called a
questions.explanation: Commercial banks are the primary institutions for accepting deposits, granting loans, and providing payment services.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: An account that allows customers to withdraw money on demand using a cheque, but usually earns little or no interest, is a
questions.explanation: A current account permits frequent withdrawals via cheque and is mainly used by businesses for daily transactions.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: An account designed for regular savings that earns interest, but with some restrictions on frequent withdrawals, is a
questions.explanation: A savings account encourages saving and pays interest, though it typically restricts the number or size of withdrawals compared to a current account.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The system by which banks settle cheques drawn on one another is called the
questions.explanation: The clearing house allows banks to exchange and settle cheques and other instruments drawn on each other efficiently.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The bank that acts as banker to the government and other commercial banks, and controls the money supply, is the
questions.explanation: The central bank (e.g., the Central Bank of Nigeria) regulates the banking system, controls money supply, and acts as banker of last resort.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A bank primarily involved in providing long-term capital and specialist advisory services to businesses, especially for large investments, is a
questions.explanation: Merchant/investment banks focus on corporate finance, underwriting, and long-term funding rather than everyday retail banking.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: An agreement in which one party (the insured) pays a sum (premium) to another (the insurer) who agrees to compensate for a specified loss is called
questions.explanation: Insurance is a risk-sharing arrangement where the insured pays premiums in exchange for compensation if a specified loss occurs.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The insurance principle stating that the insured should not profit from a claim, but should only be restored to their original financial position, is called
questions.explanation: Indemnity ensures compensation only restores the insured to their pre-loss position, without allowing profit from a claim.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The insurance principle requiring both parties to disclose all material facts honestly when arranging a policy is called
questions.explanation: Utmost good faith (uberrima fides) obliges both insurer and insured to reveal all relevant facts truthfully.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The insurance principle requiring that the insured must stand to lose financially if the insured event occurs is called
questions.explanation: Insurable interest means the policyholder must have a genuine financial stake in the item or life being insured.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The insurance principle allowing the insurer, after paying a claim, to take over the insured's rights of recovery against a third party is called
questions.explanation: Subrogation lets the insurer step into the insured's shoes to recover losses from a responsible third party after settling a claim.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The insurance principle concerned with identifying the direct, dominant cause of a loss for a claim to be valid is called
questions.explanation: Proximate cause identifies the most direct and effective cause of a loss, which must be an insured peril for the claim to succeed.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A type of insurance policy that pays a sum of money on the death of the insured or at the end of an agreed term is called
questions.explanation: Life assurance guarantees a payout either on death or at policy maturity, unlike general insurance which covers specific risk events only.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A type of insurance that covers ships, cargo, and freight against loss or damage during sea transport is called
questions.explanation: Marine insurance protects vessels and their cargo from risks encountered during a sea voyage.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A type of insurance that compensates for loss or damage to property caused by fire outbreaks is called
questions.explanation: Fire insurance covers financial loss resulting from damage to property caused by fire.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The storage of goods in a safe place until they are needed is called
questions.explanation: Warehousing is the aid to trade concerned with storing goods to bridge the gap between production and consumption periods.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A warehouse owned and used by an individual firm solely to store its own goods is called a
questions.explanation: A private warehouse belongs to and is used exclusively by a particular firm to store its own goods.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A warehouse where imported goods are kept, under customs supervision, until import duty is paid, is called a
questions.explanation: Bonded warehouses hold dutiable goods under customs control until the appropriate import duty is settled.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The main purpose of advertising in commerce is to
options: inform and persuade potential customers about goods and services
questions.explanation: Advertising aims to inform consumers of a product's existence and persuade them to buy it, overcoming the hindrance of knowledge.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Advertising that seeks mainly to give consumers factual details about a product's features and uses is called
questions.explanation: Informative advertising focuses on educating consumers about a product's features, rather than emotional appeal.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: An agreement between two or more parties that is enforceable by law is called a
questions.explanation: A contract is a legally binding agreement between parties, enforceable through the courts.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A definite proposal made by one party to another, showing willingness to enter into a contract, is called an
questions.explanation: An offer is a clear proposal made with the intention of forming a binding agreement once accepted.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The unconditional agreement to the exact terms of an offer, which forms a binding contract, is called
questions.explanation: Acceptance must match the offer's terms exactly and be communicated to the offeror to form a valid contract.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Something of value given by each party to a contract, such as money or goods, in exchange for a promise, is called
questions.explanation: Consideration is what each party gives or promises in a contract, and it must generally be of some value.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The legal ability of a party to enter into a binding contract is called
questions.explanation: Capacity refers to a party's legal competence to contract; minors, and persons of unsound mind, generally lack full contractual capacity.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: For a contract to be valid, its purpose and terms must be
questions.explanation: A contract must have a lawful purpose; agreements to commit illegal acts are void and unenforceable.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A contract can be discharged (brought to an end) in which of the following ways?
questions.explanation: Contracts end through full performance, mutual agreement, breach by one party, or frustration (an unforeseen event making performance impossible).

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The Latin maxim 'caveat emptor' used in the sale of goods means
options: goods once sold cannot be returned
all sales are final by law
questions.explanation: Caveat emptor places responsibility on the buyer to examine goods carefully before purchase, as sellers are not automatically liable for all defects.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A term in a contract of sale that is so essential that its breach entitles the buyer to reject the goods and terminate the contract is called a
questions.explanation: A condition is a major term of a contract; if breached, the innocent party may repudiate the contract and claim damages.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A term in a contract of sale that is less essential, whose breach entitles the buyer only to claim damages but not to reject the goods, is called a
questions.explanation: A warranty is a minor term; breaching it only gives the right to claim damages, not to reject the goods entirely.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: In a contract for the sale of specific goods, property (ownership) generally passes to the buyer when
options: payment has been fully completed only
the goods are delivered physically, regardless of intention
the parties intend it to pass
questions.explanation: Under the Sale of Goods law, ownership passes when the parties intend it to, which may be at the time of the contract or later, depending on the terms.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Consumer protection agencies exist mainly to
options: safeguard the interest and rights of consumers against exploitation
reduce the number of retailers in a country
questions.explanation: Consumer protection bodies exist to shield buyers from unfair trade practices, unsafe goods, and exploitation by sellers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: An agency responsible for regulating and enforcing standards for food, drugs, and cosmetics in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: NAFDAC (National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control) regulates food, drugs, and related products for safety and quality.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The Nigerian agency mainly responsible for setting and enforcing product quality standards is the
questions.explanation: SON develops and enforces standards for the quality of products manufactured or sold in Nigeria.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Which of the following is a basic right of the consumer?
options: The right to determine another consumer's purchase
The right to control a company's production process
The right to fix the prices of all goods in the market
The right to safety and to be protected from hazardous goods
questions.explanation: Consumer rights typically include the right to safety, information, choice, and redress, protecting buyers from harm and exploitation.
